content.intro: This lesson covers Debug and Release Build Profiles. It sits in Module 23, Compiler, Build System, and Performance, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Debug and Release Build Profiles matters when you work with measured performance and resource use. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: I/O interacts with resources outside the program and can fail for reasons the program does not control. Use Result-based error handling, portable path APIs, and explicit handling for missing or malformed input.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Debug and Release Build Profiles, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Inspect the compilation pipeline to locate a problem, then measure before optimizing. Release-mode results are different from debug-mode results.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not assume Debug and Release Build Profiles guarantees more than it actually does. Reduce a failure to a small reproducer, read the full compiler diagnostic or error value, consult the matching official reference, and change one assumption at a time.
